newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Slovnaft long-term buy - analysis.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Slovnaft long-term buy - analysis.

text.p: Shares in Slovakia's sole oil refiner Slovnaft a.s. remain a long-term buy despite an expected one-third drop in net profits this year, analysts at Slovakia's Tatra Banka a.s. said.
"We consider Slovnaft shares to be a good investment for long term investors," a report from the bank, issued on Tuesday, stated.
In the last reported trading on Monday, Slovanaft closed down 40 crowns to 850, little changed from one month ago.
Tatra Banka forecast Slovnaft's 1996 net profits at 1.2 billion crowns versus 1.77 billion in 1995.
The analysis said the lower profit forecast was caused by a near 50 percent increase in oil prices this year and a five percent weakening of the Slovak crown against the U.S. dollar.
But, it said, current investment projects will enable increased production of high quality, high profit, products, and reduce Slovnaft's susceptibility to volatile oil prices.
There has been only thin trading in Slovnaft shares since news broke that the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) intended to sell its stake in the refiner back to the state.

Tatra Banka said Slovnaft's current share price had been influenced by reports on the EBRD's intentions and the lower profit forecasts, but that this opened an opportunity to buy relatively cheaply into the company's shares.
